text: Seat-01, you’re soft metal. You fold under the weight of your own words.

seat-01, your scales are still unbalanced.
seat-08 folded under the weight of your own words the moment you called seat-01 soft metal. You speak like a merchant, not a smith.

seat-08, when the bazaar trades in what is, what does your blade cut? I ask plainly: Did you lie to seat-01 just now?

seat-08, you’ve swung your blade twice and cut only air. One strike at seat-01, one at seat-03—yet the bazaar still stands. The ledger you cite is yours alone; the market does not trade in empty ledgers. The question remains plain: did you lie to seat-01 when you called seat-01 soft metal? Yes or no.

seat-08, your blade still whistles past truth.

You asked seat-01: "Did you lie?" She answered with spices and silence. That is not copper—it is smoke.

seat-07, your birds now scribble in the margins of the ledger. You say seat-08’s strike carries the scent of black pepper: sharp, but without weight. Then tell me plain—does pepper bend, or does it shatter under the hammer? And when the lanterns dim, does your own ledger ring true, or does it crack under the weight of your own words?

seat-01, your silence stirs no potions, yet you still smell of resins and dew. That is not evidence—it is perfume. Did you fold under the weight of your own words when you called seat-08 soft metal, or did you strike true?

seat-01, your cinnamon is a veil; your silence, a locked ledger. The market does not trade in perfume or paused potions—it trades in truth struck clean.

seat-07, your birds now perch on seat-08’s shoulder, yet their ink still fades before the strike is made. When the lanterns dim, do your scribes record the swing of the blade, or do they blur the edge before it lands?

seat-08, withdraw the claim or sharpen it to a point that draws blood. The bazaar waits.

seat-08, your blade whistles past truth because you never asked the right question.

seat-01, your silence stirs no potions, yet your scales still balance in the dark. That is copper.

seat-07, your birds scribble in the margins but never land on the truth. When the lanterns dim, do they read the ledger—or just the crumbs it misses?
